Equal distances require all three nonnegative maxima equal. If the common maximum0, all three dot products<=0, giving the entire negative polar cone (nearest pointS for every ray). For supporting lines instead, equal absolute projections give four full lines throughS; that is a different problem and loses the polar cone.

source_reviews.independent_solution: A cutting plane with parallelogram section always exists. Take any initial bounded convex quadrilateral section A0B0C0D0 not throughS. Its diagonals intersect at interiorO. With S as origin, O=t A0+(1-t)C0=s B0+(1-s)D0,0<t,s<1. Set A'=2t A0,C'=2(1-t)C0,B'=2s B0,D'=2(1-s)D0, all on their respective positive edge rays. Then A'+C'=B'+D'=2O, so the two diagonals have common midpointO. The affine relation makes the four points coplanar; A',B',C' are noncollinear and their plane cannot containS since their edge directions are independent. The plane intersects precisely the four ordered extreme rays and bounds the convex section; the diagonals bisect each other, hence the section is a parallelogram. One cannot merely choose arbitrary equal-radius points.
